newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cheung Kong says rate impact limited.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong says rate impact limited.

text.p: Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd said on Wednesday that Hong Kong property prices should continue to be firm in 1997 and higher interest rates would only have a limited impact on the property market.
"Over the past year, as the Hong Kong property market grew more active, end-users have begun to purchase flats and offices more aggressively," the company said in a statement.
"The expected rise in interest rates will only have a limited effect due to the market's increased purchasing power. Property prices are expected to continue to be firm in 1997."
The U.S. Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time in more than two years on Tuesday, bringing the federal funds rate to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority responded on Wednesday with a 25 basis point rise in Liquidity Adjustment Facility rates, bringing the LAF bid rate to 4.25 percent and the offer rate to 6.25 percent.
The Hong Kong Association of Banks later raised short-term deposit rates by 25 basis points.
Several commercial banks followed suit by raising their prime rates by 25 basis points.
